# external-cluster

A cluster something else brings into existence, which this lab installs into.

<!-- Generated by nix/floe-docs.nix. Refresh: nix run .#refresh-floe-docs -->

## Inputs

| input | type | default | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| assignsLoadBalancers | boolean | `true` | Whether a `LoadBalancer` Service gets an address here.  True by default because every managed Kubernetes offering has a cloud controller that assigns one — which is the case this floe mostly covers, and the opposite of the bare Talos default.  |
| context | string | *(required)* | kubectl context this cluster answers on.  A decision, not a discovery: `cata` writes the kubeconfig under this name after fetching it, rather than taking whatever the producing tool called it. That is what keeps `KUBERNETES_CLUSTER.context` concrete (RFC 0005 §6.3) even though the cluster's endpoint is not.  |
| distribution | string | `"kubernetes"` | What it runs, for the record and for drift reporting. |
| edgeMode | one of "self", "none" | `"self"` | Who fronts it — RFC 0005 §6.4.  Never `proxy`: the lab's proxy reaches backends on its own docker network, and a cluster this lab did not create is not on it. `self` says the cluster is its own edge, which is what a managed cluster with a LoadBalancer is.  |
| kubeconfigFrom | null or (submodule) | `null` | Where this cluster's kubeconfig is published, when a state-based apply is what produced it (RFC 0003 §7).  Null for a cluster a controller in another cluster reconciles: there the kubeconfig is in a connection Secret and the lab reaches it through the management cluster's `provisions` declaration instead. One of the two has to say how the cluster becomes reachable, and a lab check refuses one that says neither — a cluster the lab deploys to and has no kubeconfig for fails at the first kubectl call with a context that does not exist.  |
| madeBy | string | *(required)* | What brings it into existence, for the operator reading a plan.  Free text and never dispatched on. A `create-cluster` step that does nothing reads as broken; one that says what it is waiting for reads as waiting.  |
| name | string | *(required)* | Cluster name, as members and the kubeconfig see it. Required. |
| podSubnet | string | *(required)* | Pod CIDR.  Required rather than defaulted, because for a cluster this lab does not create, a default would be a guess about somebody else's network that every member then renders against. Declared here and checked against the cluster it turns out to be.  |
| serviceSubnet | string | *(required)* | Service CIDR. Same reasoning as `podSubnet`. |
| version | string | `"1.31"` | Kubernetes minor version this cluster answers as. |

## Provides

| promise | signature | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cluster | KUBERNETES_CLUSTER | The cluster a member installs into: its name, version, context and address ranges. |

## Emits

| alias | kind | what it carries |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cluster | catallaxy.cluster | How a cluster is created and who fronts it — the descriptor `cata` builds it from. |
